newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba to hold parliamentary session Dec. 24.
newsitem.headline: Cuba to hold parliamentary session Dec. 24.

text.p: Cuba, a secular state that does not recognise Christmas as a holiday, is to hold its annual parliamentary session starting Dec. 24, on Christmas Eve, authorities announced on Wednesday.

The National Assembly normally meets twice a year for two or three days. This year's first session, delayed for unspecified reasons, was due to be held from Oct. 25 but was then cancelled because authorities were busy with recovery plans after Hurricane Lili swept the island on Oct. 17-18, damaging crops and buildings.

Parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon said in a statement published by state media that the first session of the year would be held on Dec. 24, followed immediately by the second session. This means parliament is likely to be sitting on Christmas Day, Dec. 25.

Although Christmas has not been celebrated for years in communist-ruled Cuba, it is unusual for the parliamentary session to be held over Christmas. Normally the assembly meets in the last days of December for its second session of the year.

Cuba is officially a lay state although many Cubans are Christians. Authorities have recently begun improving relations with the Roman Catholic Church and Pope John Paul is due to visit the Caribbean island next year.
President Fidel Castro held a historic first meeting with the pontiff at the Vatican last month.
